title: Authorization Patterns and the Authorized Reference — Pocketwire Visa Debit Card Operations Standard
content:
**Standard.** This standard covers the Pocketwire Visa Debit Card. On a purchase made with a single-use virtual card and disputed as an incorrect amount, the authorized reference is set by the pattern of authorizations on the card. A single-use card carries one purchase, so every authorization on the card belongs to that purchase.

| Authorizations on the single-use card | Pattern | Authorized reference |
|---|---|---|
| two or more, all placed on the same day | the later ones are incremental authorizations | the total of all the card's authorizations |
| two or more, placed on different days, that is not all on the same day | the later ones are re-authorizations | the largest single authorization |
| one | a single authorization | the authorization the purchase settled against |

**Records read.** The authorization holds on the card, with their dates and amounts, and the purchase's link to the authorization it settled against.

### Illustrations (hypothetical)

- **Incremental.** A restaurant authorizes 50.00 and, later the same day, a further 12.00. Both authorizations are on the same day, so the authorized reference is their total, 62.00.
- **Re-authorization.** A merchant authorizes 200.00 on 1 June and re-authorizes 240.00 on 4 June. The authorizations are on different days, so the authorized reference is the largest single authorization, 240.00.
- **Three authorizations, not all on one day.** 20.00 and 5.00 are authorized on 2 June and 22.00 on 3 June. They are not all on the same day, so the largest single authorization applies: 22.00.
- **Single.** One authorization of 35.00, which the purchase settled against. The authorized reference is 35.00.
